concerns.text: Task T021 mandates downloading and loading 'distilbert-tiny' with 'pinned revision hash'. The spec (US-2) and plan (Technical Context) require a 'small pre-trained LLM' but do not specify a model ID or revision. Hardcoding a specific model ID and revision in the task without a prior design decision (e.g., in research.md or plan.md) constitutes a silent narrowing of the FR-003 requirement to a specific implementation choice not yet validated, violating the 'No silent constitution drift' principle.

Tasks T040b, T040c, and T043 implement a 'literature-based GPU conversion factor' to estimate GPU-hours for the baseline. While the Plan.md admits this is an approximation, the Spec (FR-004) and Constitution (Principle VII) mandate measuring 'computational cost' and comparing 'CPU-seconds vs GPU-hours'. By replacing the measurement of actual GPU cost with a literature-derived estimate, the task list effectively weakens FR-004 from 'measure actual cost' to 'estimate cost via literature', which is a semantic relaxation of the requirement to empirically verify the efficiency claim.

Task T029d requires deriving the 'complexity class (Big-O)' via log-log linear regression on a single dataset generation (N=10..500). The Spec (SC-005) requires measuring the 'computational complexity class of the relationship between problem complexity and computation time'. A regression on a single curve cannot mathematically prove the asymptotic complexity class (e.g., distinguishing O(n log n) from O(n^1.5)) without varying the algorithm or solver. This task delivers a statistical fit, not the required complexity class verification, silently weakening SC-005.

Task T048 is marked as 'unimplemented' (checkbox unchecked) in the provided text, yet it is the sole task addressing the Spec's Edge Case: 'What happens if the symbolic planner generates a sub-goal that is logically impossible... The system must detect the logical contradiction'. Leaving this task unimplemented while claiming to satisfy the Edge Case requirement is a direct violation of the spec's acceptance criteria for US-2.

Tasks T008a and T008c rely on 'literature-based TDP values' for CPU calibration because hardware sensors are unavailable. Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) requires results to be reproducible on a fresh runner. If the 'literature value' is not pinned to a specific CPU model ID (which varies across GitHub Actions runners), the energy calculation becomes non-reproducible. The task does not mandate detecting the runner's specific CPU model to select the correct literature value, creating a silent drift from the Reproducibility principle.
